Compiles a plain-language invention idea into requirements, schematics, tests, and a manufacturing package. (Proposed capability.) A requirements-to-reality compiler would turn an idea paragraph into a full engineering package. Pieces exist (requirements extraction, generative CAD, test generation); the end-to-end compiler is simulated in demos. Status: simulated. Capability status: PROPOSED. This database describes a proposed capability, not a completed product. Status taxonomy used throughout: speculative (no demonstrated path), simulated (works in simulation only), experimentally-demonstrated (lab demo exists), independently-verified (reproduced by a third party). Generating a design cannot make impossible physics possible; every record states which status its claims carry. Capability status for this tool: simulated.

title: Requirements-to-Reality Compiler — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Compiles a plain-language invention idea into requirements, schematics, tests, and a manufacturing package. (Proposed capability.)
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Teaching ladder for Requirements-to-Reality Compiler, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Idea-to-requirements extraction). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Idea-to-requirements extraction and Schematic and CAD drafting. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Requirements-to-CAD generation engine) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else. Capability status for this tool: simulated.
